question: Does the existing synthetic-trained corner CNN offer stable, visually useful proposals on the fixed real-photo cohort? Swapping A/B mask names must not move actual visible junctions.

protocol.model: Frozen 880466-parameter MobileNetV3-small proposal network, trained on synthetic corners with ImageNet initialization.
protocol.controls: Compare one synthetic forward pass exactly with the existing infer helper at float16 storage precision. Require immutable checkpoint, native crop/mask/coverage, and exact A/B complementation. The two neural passes share identical RGB and validity.
protocol.interpretation: One-to-one phase agreement measures stability, not real corner accuracy. Compare raw proposals and the existing synthetic-development-selected 9px refinement. No per-photo method, threshold, checkpoint or reference-dependent proposal selection.

evaluation: Keep all 32 photos, including six unresolved crops. Store both heatmap heads and raw/refined proposals for all 26 fixed crops. Inspect every source/crop/mask/proposal panel. No ground-truth junction coordinates, new solve, training, production integration or accuracy claim.
limitations: The existing CNN saw procedural photographs, not this real development cohort.
These repeatedly inspected real photos are not an untouched holdout.
The mask itself can miss true material boundaries or contain printed-ink artifacts.
Phase stability is necessary for reliable proposals but does not prove useful graph connectivity or legal cutting paths.
